To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) GCA is a powerful technique to support the context-adaptive adaptation of applications and (2) GCA can be applied successfully to mobile cloud applications.
GCA is a promising concept that allows to automatically identify the context of mobile devices and to adapt (mobile) applications based on this knowledge.

(i) context-awareness is a key factor in mobile cloud computing, (ii) the GCA approach is suitable to support context-aware adaptation of (mobile cloud) applications, and (iii) GCA is a promising approach to enable context-aware adaptation of mobile applications in mobile cloud computing environments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How can we model the context of mobile devices and their users?
the development of a novel approach to support the adaptation of mobile applications to their context, which is a prerequisite for mobile applications in MCC environments.
the development of a novel context-aware middleware for mobile cloud computing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach is able to predict the context with a high accuracy and is therefore able to provide a good basis for the adaptation of mobile applications.
GCA is a powerful and promising approach to support the development of context-adaptive mobile applications.

GCA can be applied to a wide range of applications, but it is still an open question how to efficiently and effectively implement the GCA process in a way that is both scalable and efficient in terms of time and space.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GCA allows us to automatically generate context-aware application adaptations for MCC environments.
GCA is a powerful approach to facilitate the adaptation of (cloud-enabled) applications to their context and thus enables the development of highly adaptive applications.
GCA is able to provide a solid foundation for the development and deployment of mobile applications that can be easily adapted to the current and future context of the user.
The main takeaway from our work is that
context adaptation is feasible for mobile cloud applications, which is confirmed by our evaluation.
context-adaptive mobile applications can be developed in a generic manner and that the adaptation process can be automated to a great extent.

GCA can be used to improve the performance of mobile devices by offloading resource-demanding parts of mobile applications to the cloud or nearby devices, and to reduce the energy consumption of the mobile device.
